subtopic: Reflection of Sound — Echo, Reverberation and SONAR
stem:
What is the use of the device shown in the given below image?

(The figure illustrates SONAR in two modes. In the 'Passive' panel a submarine listens to the sound waves coming from another submarine. In the 'Active' panel a ship/submarine sends out sound waves underwater which strike a submarine and the reflected waves return to the source.)

The separation between T and C in the figure given is

(The figure is a graph of density versus distance for a sound wave — a sine curve. C marks a crest, the point of maximum density, i.e. a compression, and T marks a trough, the point of minimum density, i.e. a rarefaction. C and T are adjacent on the curve.)

subtopic: Reflection of Sound — Echo, Reverberation and SONAR
stem:
While doing experiment on verifying the law of reflection of sound, four students measured the angles i and r as shown in the diagram below. The correct measurement of the angle of incidence and angle of reflection has been done by student

(Each diagram A, B, C, D shows two tubes meeting at a wall with a dotted normal line, and the angles i and r marked. In diagram A both i and r are measured between the tubes and the normal. In diagram B angle i is measured from the wall and r from the normal. In diagram C angle i is measured from the normal and r from the wall. In diagram D both i and r are measured from the wall.)

When a pulse produced in a string moves through it and strikes a rigid pole, it is reflected back and the shape of the reflected pulse resembles the shape given in

(The options are four waveform diagrams of a pulse on a string near a rigid (fixed) wall. (i): an upright crest reflected, travelling to the left (away from the wall). (ii): an inverted (downward) trough travelling to the left, away from the wall. (iii): an upright crest near the wall moving to the right. (iv): an inverted trough moving to the right, toward the wall.)

subtopic: Reflection of Sound — Echo, Reverberation and SONAR
stem:
To verify the law of reflection of sound, the set-up of the arrangement needed is the one shown in figure

(The options are four set-ups near a reflecting surface (hatched wall) with a vertical normal line. In set-up A (and C) the two tubes are inclined symmetrically on either side of the normal, so a definite angle of incidence and reflection can be measured. In set-up B (and D) the two tubes are vertical, perpendicular to the wall, giving zero angle of incidence — unsuitable for verifying the law at an angle.)

Which characteristic of sound is represented in the given image?

(The figure shows two waveforms of wave-disturbance versus time with the same frequency but different heights. The upper wave labelled 'Soft sound' has a small height, while the lower wave labelled 'Louder sound' has a much larger height.)

subtopic: Reflection of Sound — Echo, Reverberation and SONAR
stem:
The given image shows the phenomena of:

(The figure shows a flat board at the top. Two tubes are inclined on either side of a vertical normal line, meeting the board at one point, with equal angles i and i marked from the normal. One tube leads from a ticking watch (the sound source); the other tube leads to an ear (the listener).)

subtopic: Reflection of Sound — Echo, Reverberation and SONAR
stem:
Four students after conducting an experiment on reflection of sound marked the angle of incidence, angle of reflection as follows. Which one is correct?

(Each diagram A, B, C, D shows an incident ray striking a surface and a reflected ray leaving it, with a dotted normal. In diagram A both the angle of incidence i and angle of reflection r are marked between the rays and the normal, on opposite sides, and are equal. In the other diagrams the angles are marked from the reflecting surface or on the wrong sides.)

What is the velocity of the pulse for the slinky indicated in the figure below? Given that the pulse took 5 seconds to travel from A to B and then back to A.

(The figure shows a hand holding one end of a slinky. The near end is marked A and the far end B, with the distance from A to B marked as 10 m.)

subtopic: Reflection of Sound — Echo, Reverberation and SONAR
stem:
Which of the following is the correct experimental set-up for verification of laws of reflection of sound?

(The options are four set-ups A, B, C, D. Each has a reflecting board at the top, two inclined tubes meeting at the board, and a vertical screen/barrier placed below along the normal to block sound travelling directly between the tubes. In set-up A the two tubes touch the board at one point on its surface (the point of incidence) with the screen below; the other set-ups have the tubes meeting away from the board surface or are otherwise incorrect.)

subtopic: Reflection of Sound — Echo, Reverberation and SONAR
stem:
Four students after conducting an experiment on reflection of sound marked the angle of incidence and angle of reflection as follows. Which one is correct?

(Each diagram i, ii, iii, iv shows a reflecting board with two tubes meeting at it and a vertical normal. In diagram (iv) the angle of incidence i is marked between the left tube and the normal and the angle of reflection r between the right tube and the normal, on opposite sides and equal. In (i) both angles are marked on the same side of the normal; in (ii) the angles are measured from the board surface; in (iii) the angles are marked incorrectly.)

If the pulse hits at the fixed end as shown in the diagram A, the immediately reflected pulse is:

(Diagram A shows a string with an upward pulse moving toward a rigid (fixed) wall. The options are four diagrams: (i) an inverted (downward) pulse located right next to the wall, moving away from it; (ii) an upright pulse next to the wall; (iii) an inverted pulse far from the wall, moving away; (iv) an upright pulse far from the wall.)

The pitch of the two signals A and B shown below are \(P_A\) and \(P_B\) respectively. Then

(The figure shows two waveforms. Signal A has many closely-spaced waves — a high frequency. Signal B has fewer, widely-spaced waves — a low frequency.)

In the curve figure, half the wavelength is

(The figure shows one complete sine wave drawn over a horizontal axis from A to E. Going left to right: A is at the start on the axis, B is the point on the axis below the crest (one-quarter of the wave), C is the zero-crossing in the middle (half the wave), D is the point on the axis below the trough (three-quarters of the wave) and E is the end of the wave on the axis.)
